fine_trace.note: The Ruby input uses return *x, causing the compiler to emit OP_ARYSPLAT for an input-controlled expression.
The VM executes OP_ARYSPLAT on the object supplied by the input, entering array splat conversion.

fine_trace.code: mrb_value ary = mrb_funcall_argv(mrb, v, MRB_SYM(to_a), 0, NULL);
fine_trace.note: For the crafted object, splat conversion invokes the Ruby to_a method, re-entering the VM before the outer OP_ARYSPLAT handler finishes.
Recursive calls made from to_a can exhaust the current callinfo array and reallocate c->cibase while an older mrb_vm_exec frame still keeps a local ci pointer into the previous allocation.
After mrb_ary_splat returns, dispatch resumes using the outer frame's stale local ci pointer, which may reference freed callinfo storage after the reallocation.
